scenarios.description: Drive the production desktop frog renderer, preload and stdio peer under sandboxed Linux Electron.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: After adopting a frog, start a recording from the frog and save an eligible milestone recording.
prerequisites: The built Desktop frontend, its locked Electron runtime, Xvfb, a working Electron sandbox and xwininfo.

runner.instructions: After building the Desktop frontend, run xvfb-run -a node --experimental-strip-types --test onboarding/electron/desktop-frog/smoke.ts from the repository root.

expectedEvidence: The frog renders its name and updates the displayed shortcut.
A hidden frog cannot start capture. Starting from a visible frog unmaps the window before the start intent, and the current parent projection determines when it returns.

New achievements announce 10, 30 and 60 saved recordings, equip the new accessory, and fit in the desktop frog window. Equipment-only updates do not replay the celebration. Reduce Motion keeps the achievement and accessory visible and hides streamers.
limits: The coordinator is a fixture. A real Xorg or Hyprland desktop, installed package and native Record action require separate acceptance.

scenarios.description: Recognize the fatal Chromium sandbox diagnostic when the Linux Desktop frog cannot start.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Open an adopted Desktop frog and inspect the Apparent log if its Electron child exits with no usable sandbox.
prerequisites: The repository's normal native Cargo test prerequisites on Linux.

runner.instructions: Run cargo test --locked frog_sandbox_tests from the repository root.

expectedEvidence: The observer recognizes a fatal sandbox message from a signaled child, including a marker split across reads.
Repeated markers produce one diagnostic, unrelated stderr is ignored, and a confirmed failure refuses another launch.
limits: The subprocess is synthetic. Verify the installed launcher and its fixed diagnostic in a supported isolated Linux desktop.

scenarios.description: Add the installed Nightly app to Screen & System Audio Recording from the compact permissions guide.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Choose Open Settings on the onboarding Screen & System Audio Recording row. Drag the Nightly app just above the first Add (+) button, then enable access and follow the macOS reopen prompt if shown.
prerequisites: An isolated macOS desktop with the signed Nightly candidate installed and a fresh permission state.
expectedEvidence: The card is compact and keeps the permission controls usable at normal and small display sizes in light and dark appearance.
The drop adds the correct Nightly app and the onboarding row reflects the grant after macOS reopens the app.
A cancelled drop leads to the permission switch or the keyboard-accessible Add (+) action.
limits: The geometry script and synthetic Electron permission smoke do not prove the live System Settings drop or grant.

scenarios.description: Choose standalone Fn with a physical keyboard in the macOS Electron shortcut recorder.
scenarios.userEntryPoint: Open the welcome tour from Settings → About in a fresh test profile. On Test your recording shortcut, choose Change shortcut and press and release Fn while the recorder is focused. Test Fn with another press and release, then select Use shortcut.
prerequisites: The installed candidate, a Mac with an Fn or Globe key in an approved isolated environment, and the app's normal Accessibility and recording grants.
A test profile with a non-Fn Record shortcut. Exercise both guided-practice preference values with Desktop Frog disabled.

runner.instructions: Run cargo test onboarding_selects_fn_after_release_from_the_current_focused_editor on macOS for the synthetic CoreGraphics regression. Exercise the installed tour manually for physical input.

expectedEvidence: The held Fn key does not select a shortcut. Its release saves Record as Fn and returns to the test. The next press and release highlights the key and pebble. Use shortcut closes setup without opening the target picker or starting capture.
Fn used with another key, or with focus in another app, does not save Fn in the editor.
limits: The automated regression injects CoreGraphics events and a focus predicate. It does not establish physical Fn delivery, installed window focus, or macOS Globe settings.
